facts.statement: Huinculsaurus is known from a single species, Huinculsaurus montesi, based on five partial vertebrae.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Huinculsaurus montesi, known from five partial vertebrae.

facts.statement: The fossils of Huinculsaurus were discovered around 1991 in the Huincul Formation in Neuquén, Argentina, near the site of the Ilokelesia holotype.
facts.quote: The only known fossils of Huinculsaurus was discovered around 1991 in the Huincul Formation, about 10 m away from where the Ilokelesia holotype was discovered in the Argentine Province of Neuquén.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Huinculsaurus were mechanically separated during preparation before the genus was formally published in 2020.
facts.quote: The vertebrae were mechanically separated during preparation before being formally published in 2020.

facts.statement: The species name montesi honors Eduardo Montes, a fossil preparator who died shortly before the official publication of the species.
facts.quote: The species epithet was given in honor of Eduardo Montes, a technician and fossil preparator at the Carmen Funes Museum, who helped prepare the specimen and died shortly before its official publication.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the holotype was an immature individual because its vertebrae were not fully fused.
facts.quote: It is believed to have been an immature individual because the centra are not fully fused to the neural arches.

facts.statement: Researchers estimate that Huinculsaurus was around 3.42 meters long in life.
facts.quote: Researchers have estimated that in life, it was around 3.42 m long.

facts.statement: Huinculsaurus is distinguished from other theropods by unique vertebral features such as elongated articular facets, pneumatic foramina, and an accessory lamina.
facts.quote: Huinculsaurus is distinguished from all other theropods by several autapomorphic features of the vertebrae including elongated articular facets on the prezygapophyses, pneumatic foramina on the underside of the dorsal vertebrae, and an accessory lamina on the dorsal neural arches.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses suggest Huinculsaurus is a close relative of the Late Jurassic theropod Elaphrosaurus.
facts.quote: In both analyses, Huinculsaurus was found to be a close relative of the Late Jurassic theropod Elaphrosaurus, which lived more than 60 million years earlier.

facts.statement: The precise classification of Huinculsaurus is difficult because its vertebrae share similarities with both Noasauridae and Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: They remarked that the vertebrae of Huinculsaurus share many similarities with Noasauridae as well as Abelisauridae, which make its precise classification difficult.

facts.statement: Huinculsaurus is classified within the family Noasauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Noasauridae

facts.statement: Huinculsaurus is assigned to the subfamily Elaphrosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Elaphrosaurinae

facts.statement: The subfamily Elaphrosaurinae includes graceful theropods of small to medium size, such as Elaphrosaurus and Limusaurus.
facts.quote: Esta subfamilia incluye terópodos gráciles y de pequeño a mediano tamaño, como Elaphrosaurus y Limusaurus, conocidos del Jurásico Superior de África y Asia, respectivamente.

facts.statement: Including Huinculsaurus in Elaphrosaurinae extends the known temporal range of this subfamily to the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: La inclusión de Huinculsaurus en este grupo extiende la presencia temporal de los elafrosaurinos hasta el Cretácico Superior, siendo el miembro más reciente conocido de esta subfamilia.

facts.statement: Huinculsaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Albian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous (Albian),

facts.statement: Huinculsaurus lived in the middle Cretaceous, approximately 97 to 93 million years ago during the Cenomanian, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace unos 97 a 93 millones de años durante el Cenomaniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Huinculsaurus is the latest known member of the Elaphrosaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Es el elafrosaurino más tardío conocido, data del período Cretácico superior.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Huinculsaurus spans from 110.1 to 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Huincul Formation, where Huinculsaurus was found, consists of yellowish and greenish fine-to-medium grain sandstones, some containing volcanic ash.
facts.quote: The Huincul Formation is composed of yellowish and greenish sandstones of fine-to-medium grain, some of which are tuffaceous.

facts.statement: The environment of the Huincul Formation is thought to have been arid with ephemeral or seasonal streams.
facts.quote: The Huincul Formation is thought to represent an arid environment with ephemeral or seasonal streams.

facts.statement: Fossilized pollen from the Huincul Formation indicates the presence of hornworts, liverworts, ferns, conifers, and some flowering plants.
facts.quote: Fossilised pollen indicates a wide variety of plants were present in the Huincul Formation. A study of the El Zampal section of the formation found hornworts, liverworts, ferns, conifers, and some angiosperms (flowering plants).

facts.statement: Huinculsaurus coexisted with the abelisaurid Ilokelesia at the same locality.
facts.quote: Huinculsaurus is known to have coexisted with the abelisaurid Ilokelesia, which was found at the same locality.

facts.statement: The Huincul Formation contains fossils of titanosaurs like Argentinosaurus and rebbachisaurids like Cathartesaura.
facts.quote: Sauropods are represented by the titanosaurs Bustingorrytitan, Choconsaurus, Chucarosaurus, and Argentinosaurus as well as the rebbachisaurids Astigmasaura, Cathartesaura, Cienciargentina, and Sidersaura.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Huinculsaurus may have occupied a different ecological niche, possibly as an omnivore or herbivore with a cursorial lifestyle, due to its coexistence with large predators.
facts.quote: La coexistencia de Huinculsaurus con estos grandes depredadores sugiere una posible partición ecológica, donde Huinculsaurus podría haber ocupado un nicho diferente, posiblemente como un omnívoro o herbívoro, adaptado a una dieta distinta y a un estilo de vida más cursorial.

facts.statement: Hypotheses regarding the evolutionary relationships of Huinculsaurus are considered preliminary due to a lack of small ceratosaur fossils.
facts.quote: However, the relative lack of available fossils from small ceratosaurs makes their hypotheses about its evolutionary relationships very preliminary.
